title: Substantive procedures — Pioneer Components
instructions: For each risk at **Pioneer Components**, select the most effective substantive procedure, then identify the guidance governing a scope issue.

exhibits.title: Risks identified
exhibits.content:
1. Unrecorded accounts payable at year-end.
2. Fictitious sales recorded in the last week of the year.
3. Obsolete inventory carried at full cost.
4. Equipment retired during the year but still recorded.
5. Receivables that don't exist.
6. Undisclosed pending litigation.

parts.prompt: Select the most effective procedure for each risk.

rows.label: 1. Unrecorded payables
rows.answer: Examine disbursements after year-end and trace to year-end payables

rows.label: 2. Fictitious year-end sales
rows.answer: Vouch year-end sales to shipping documents and review subsequent credit memos

rows.label: 3. Obsolete inventory
rows.answer: Compare inventory costs with subsequent selling prices and review slow-moving reports

rows.label: 4. Unrecorded retirements
rows.answer: Review insurance and property tax records and scrap sales

rows.label: 6. Undisclosed litigation
rows.answer: Send a letter of audit inquiry to outside legal counsel

parts.prompt: Pioneer's outside counsel refuses to respond to the inquiry letter. Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) governs the effect on the report?

excerpts.text: A lawyer's refusal to furnish the information requested in an inquiry letter, either in writing or orally, is a limitation on the scope of the audit sufficient to preclude an unmodified opinion.
If management refuses to allow the auditor to send a confirmation request, the auditor should inquire about management's reasons and seek evidence of their validity.
The auditor should request written representations from management with appropriate responsibilities for the financial statements.
The auditor should perform audit procedures designed to obtain evidence that all subsequent events requiring adjustment or disclosure have been identified.

parts.explanation: AU-C 501 treats a lawyer's refusal to respond as a scope limitation.
